2. Reachable-set representations

Compare five set representations on one square

Ready · analytic illustration

At d=(1,0), Q support is 1 and the enclosing disk support is √2. At d=(1,1), both supports equal 2. Q⊂E⊂[-√2,√2]². The H/V polytope, zonotope, parallelotope, and box are exact here. The ellipsoid is an outer enclosure. Actual operation support depends on the inventory profile and request.

RepresentationCost for common operationsInclusion and conversion limits
H/V polytopeH membership scans its inequalities; V support scans its vertices. H support uses an optimization solve.H↔V conversion can increase the number of rows or vertices exponentially in dimension.
ZonotopeSupport is linear in the number of generators; membership solves for generator coefficients.Generator reduction can produce an outer cover and lose tightness. The square fixture uses only two generators and needs no reduction.
ParallelotopeMembership maps through a basis solve; support evaluates the generator directions.Affine images are compact when the basis is nonsingular. Singular images need a general set representation or a solver.
EllipsoidDense-matrix membership and support use quadratic forms and matrix-vector products.Support-based enclosures can be conservative; the disk E contains Q and is not equal to it.
BoxMembership and directional support scale linearly with dimension.An outer box can lose coordinate correlations. It equals Q only for this axis-aligned fixture.

These are qualitative operation costs and representation limits, not benchmark timings. The next chapter runs actual installed consumers for box, parallelotope, zonotope, and ellipsoid methods; each result keeps its own relation and assurance.

Reproduce this result

Full input description and JSON

Q=[-1,1]^2. H rows: ±x<=1, ±y<=1. V corners: (±1,±1). Z center 0, generators e1,e2. Parallelotope A[-1,1]^2 with A=I. E={x:xᵀx<=2}. All centers are zero, generator coefficients lie in [−1,1], and support is evaluated in directions (1,0) and (1,1).

Open the structured chapter manifest JSON

python3 scripts/reports/learning_geometry_toy.py

Expected output

d=(1.0, 0.0); exact_square=1; outer_disk=1.41421
d=(1.0, 1.0); exact_square=2; outer_disk=2
polytope=exact zonotope=exact parallelotope=exact ellipsoid=outer box=exact
Q subset E; E subset [-sqrt(2),sqrt(2)]^2; Q is [-1,1]^2

Intermediate geometry. At d=(1,0), Q support is 1 and the enclosing disk support is √2. At d=(1,1), both supports equal 2. Q⊂E⊂[-√2,√2]².

Support limits. The square, zonotope, parallelotope, and box describe the same exact set in this example. The disk is an outer enclosure. No CSL API is called by this script.
